# Nova Browser

> A free, open-source desktop browser with local AI, workspaces, network filtering, encrypted sync, and native MCP integration.

Nova is available for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows x64, and Linux x64. It is built with Electron, React and TypeScript and licensed under MIT.

## Features

- Local AI: supported models run on the device through WebGPU after a model download. Availability and performance depend on compatible hardware. External agents and providers have their own data handling.
- Organization: workspaces, vertical or horizontal tabs, split view, and tab hibernation.
- Privacy: network filtering blocks ads and known trackers.
- Sync: bookmarks and passwords are encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM using your Nova Cloud account. Pairing devices using a sync code is not available in this build.
- Extensions: Chrome Web Store extension support; compatibility varies by extension.
- Agents: a built-in local MCP server connects compatible coding agents.

## Official links

- Website: https://nova-browser.org/
- Source code: https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser
- Latest release and installers: https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/releases/latest
- Report an issue: https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/issues
- License: https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/blob/main/LICENSE

The website offers English and Turkish copy. Download the installer matching your operating system and processor architecture from official GitHub releases.

## Local AI requirements

An initial model download is required. Model support, speed and memory usage depend on the device. Local model inference runs on the device; this does not imply that all browser networking or external agent services run offline.

## Sync

Sync bookmarks, passwords, and preferences across computers using your Nova Cloud account with client-side AES-256-GCM encryption. Pairing devices using a sync code is not available in this build.
